text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Monthly inflation in Bulgaria in May is expected to rise to two percent from -0.7 percent in April, statistics experts forecast.
-- Bulgaria's exports rose by 10 percent in the first quarter of this year against the same period in 1996, Trade Minister Daniela Bobeva said.

-- Bulgaria's interim government has prepared a letter of intent to approach the World Bank for a $170 million FESAL loan, which should be used for structural reform, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament tentatively approved a bill to raise the monthly tax-free allowance to 50,000 levs from 25,000 levs.
-- Germany's Heidelberger Zement AG was approved as buyer of a 51 percent stake in Bulgaria's Zlatna Panega cement maker for $26 million, the construction ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's Geology Committee said US Texaco Inc intended to sell the exploration rights on gas deposits near the northeast Bulgarian Black Sea port of Varna.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov formally asked Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov to form a government, following his coalition's victory in April 19 parliamentary elections. Kostov is expected to present the new cabinet on Monday.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had started negotiations with foreign firms, including Belgium's Union Miniere SA, Swiss firm Glencore International and Korea's Daewoo, interested in buying 56 percent of the MDK copper smelter in Pirdop.
-- The Swiss Surito Investments AG said it had submitted a bid to the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) to buy Bulgaria's First Private Bank, which was placed in receivership by the BNB last year.
-- Bulgaria had a $200 million commodity turnover with Cyprus last year, a Cyprus Trade and Industrial Chamber official said.
